question: A 21-year-old man comes to the physician for a follow-up examination. Four days ago, he injured his right knee while playing soccer. Increased laxity of the right knee joint is noted when the knee is flexed to 30° and an abducting force is applied to the lower leg. The examination finding in this patient is most likely caused by damage to which of the following structures?
reasoning_chain: CHAIN: Injury to the right knee while playing soccer -> increased laxity of the right knee joint -> laxity noted when knee flexed to 30° and an abducting force applied -> damage to a stabilizing structure -> possible damage to a ligament -> 70%
analysis: The increased laxity of the right knee joint with abduction force applied at 30° flexion suggests damage to the lateral collateral ligament (LCL). The LCL provides stability to the outer side of the knee and is commonly injured during activities that involve a force pushing the knee inward.
